hero.label: Education · Free resources
hero.title:
A weekly hang,
not a class.
hero.lede: The Barbershop is where Sean's students at IU meet, listen, talk, and play. Here it houses his teaching: the philosophy, the studio, the outreach, and a library of free resources for any drummer who wants them.

philosophy.title: How Sean teaches
philosophy.lede: Your instrument is a megaphone to your soul.
paragraphs: Time, touch, reading, vocabulary: they matter because they let you take care of the band. A drummer who makes the bass player comfortable, who hears the pianist's left hand and stays out of its way, who knows the melody of the tune they're playing, is a drummer who gets called back. That is the whole job, and it is a joyful one.

Lessons are built around the bandstand, not the practice room. Students transcribe, they play with records, they play with each other, and they play in public as early as Sean can get them there. Mistakes are information. Ego is noise.
The Barbershop itself is the weekly hang: the whole studio in one room, listening to something, arguing about it, and then playing it. Nobody is graded. Everybody plays.
philosophy.quote: Don’t let the notes ruin the music… try to hear it before you see it.

study.title: Study with Sean at Jacobs
study.blurb: Jazz drumset, Indiana University Jacobs School of Music, Bloomington.
study.text: The Jacobs School offers Bachelor of Music, Master of Music, and Doctor of Music degrees in Jazz Studies, and drummers in the program study with Sean. Applications go through Jacobs, not through this site; the links below are the official ones.
study.also: Not headed to Jacobs? Sean has run the Sean Dobbins Virtual Drum Set Intensive online since 2019, open to drummers anywhere.
